methodology: The mechanical properties of the mortar composites were investigated using a four-probe method for estimating their piezoresistive response. research_objective: The aim of this study was to accelerate progress in the field of material development, providing a deeper insight into the correlation among cementitious composite preparation, admixture dispersion quality, cementitious composite microstructure, and mechanical as well as self-sensing properties.

key_findings.finding: The incorporation of carbon nanotubes and carbon microfibers into mortar composites resulted in enhanced mechanical properties, including increased flexural and compressive strengths.

The combination of dispersant agents along with low content of CNTs and CMFs by weight of cement (bwoc) led to a smooth and reversible change in electrical resistivity versus compression loading, indicating self-sensing behavior.
CNTs and CMFs enhance the mechanical properties of composites, leading to improved construction integrity and self-sensing capabilities.
CNTs have high electrical conductivity, which can potentially reinforce piezoresistive properties of cementitious materials.
Silica fume enhances the strength of concrete due to its spherical-shaped particles that penetrate into cementitious composites, increasing the distance between fillers.
CNTs' dispersion is improved by adding silica fume and using polycarboxylate-based stabilizers without deteriorating or destroying their structures.

The study discusses the differences between covalent and non-covalent functionalization of carbon nanotubes (CNTs). Covalent functionalization involves direct attachment of chemical groups to CNT surfaces, while non-covalent functionalization relies on physical interactions such as hydrogen bonding, π-π stacking, and Van der Waals forces.
